status.description: hit = an immutable archived row was served. unavailable/error = nothing was served; see coverage.reason_code. A `miss` never reaches the public surface.

accepted_fields.description: The request fields this endpoint accepts, echoed on unserved responses so an agent can self-correct.

population_count.description: Null means the legacy response did not record this count; null is never equivalent to zero.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable cause, present whenever status is unavailable or error. Request-side codes (fixture_*/player_*/entity_*/unsupported_parameter) mean the caller can fix the request; the gateway answers them with HTTP 400 (missing/ambiguous/unsupported) or 404 (not_found). archive_row_missing (HTTP 503) and archive_error (HTTP 502) are on our side. None of these calls is billed.

FixtureSelector.description: Supply an exact id or enough team/date information to resolve exactly one fixture. Multiple supplied selectors are conjunctive. Ambiguous requests return candidates and do not call a provider.

event.description: Fixture label such as Brazil vs Morocco.

forecast.description: The model's ORIGINAL pre-kickoff Dixon-Coles forecast, preserved exactly as it was computed before the match. Nothing is recomputed at request time and no post-match information leaks in; forecast_integrity states whether the stored timestamp is genuinely pre-kickoff.

confidence.description: Model self-assessed confidence in [0,1]; 0.15 for seed-only forecasts.

data_source.description: How the pre-kickoff model was fed. seed = no FIFA World Cup 2026 result existed yet for at least one side, so the model used the FIFA-ranking seed prior (typical for every team's first match; confidence 0.15). blend = tournament results blended with the seed prior (confidence rises with games played). results = fitted on tournament results only. A seed forecast is the intended archived answer, not a placeholder; archive.notes carries the same explanation on every forecast hit.

GatewayError.description: Transport envelope of every non-2xx answer (machina-client-api core/worldcup/gateway.py). Unserved archived answers (selector missing or ambiguous, unknown fixture, unsupported parameter, capability gap) are typed here and are never billed.

type.description: Gateway classification of an unserved answer (absent on auth/credit errors).

billed.description: Always false on an unserved answer: no credit debit, no ZeroClick usage.

accepted_fields.description: Request fields the endpoint accepts; use them to correct the call.

skill_card.headline: Brazil and Morocco Share the Points in Hard-Fought 1-1 World Cup Draw
standout_players: Ismael Saibari (Morocco) - Scored the opening goal with a clever lob and remained a constant threat.
Vinícius Júnior (Brazil) - Provided the moment of magic needed to equalize for his side.
Alisson Becker (Brazil) - Secured the draw with vital late-game heroics in stoppage time.
skill_card.summary: Brazil and Morocco played out an intense 1-1 draw in their opening match of the 2026 FIFA World Cup at MetLife Stadium. Morocco opened the scoring in the 21st minute when Ismael Saibari intercepted a loose ball and lobbed Alisson Becker. Brazil responded just 11 minutes later through a spectacular individual effort from Vinícius Júnior. Despite late pressure and a dramatic double save by Alisson in the 98th minute, neither side could find a winner, leaving both teams with a point in Group C.
turning_points: 21st minute: Ismael Saibari capitalizes on a midfield error, lobbing Alisson Becker to put Morocco ahead.
32nd minute: Vinícius Júnior cuts inside and curls a brilliant shot into the top corner to level the score for Brazil.
90+8th minute: Alisson Becker produces a crucial double save to deny Morocco a dramatic late winner.
skill_card.what_it_means: The draw leaves both teams with one point in Group C, demonstrating Morocco's ability to compete with elite opposition and serving as an early wake-up call for Brazil.

503.description: A valid selector for which the archive holds no row (coverage.reason_code = archive_row_missing). Retry later. Never billed.

servers.description: Upstream Machina API used by the ZeroClick catalog importer; not the buyer-facing gateway.

x-publication.manual_gate: Authorized dashboard re-import and post-import verification are required; changing openApiUrl alone does not publish or overwrite the catalog.

x-transport-contract: Since 1.5.0 every 200 schema and example describes the body exactly as api.machina.gg and the ZeroClick storefront deliver it: the transport envelope {status:'success', meta:{code:200}, data:<endpoint payload>}. The endpoint payload (archive, coverage, warnings and the endpoint-specific fields) is what the workflow returns; the envelope is platform-owned (machina-client-api SystemResponse). Every non-2xx uses the GatewayError envelope {status:'error', meta:{code}, data:{}, error:{code, type, reason_code, message, billed:false, accepted_fields, candidates, archive, coverage}}. Unserved answers (archive.status unavailable/error) are mapped by the gateway to HTTP 400/404/503/502 before any debit and are never billed, neither on Machina credits nor as ZeroClick usage. Before 1.5.0 the 200 schemas described only the inner data block (ZeroClick report, 2026-09-22).
